itinerary.title: Arrival in Guwahati & Transfer to Shillong (3-4hrs/100kms)
itinerary.desc: Arrive in Guwahati via flight or train. From there, transfer to Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, which takes approximately 3-4 hours by road. Upon arrival in Shillong, check in to your hotel, relax, and freshen up. In the evening, explore Police Bazar, a lively market area, and take a peaceful stroll around Ward’s Lake. Enjoy some local delicacies for dinner and stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Shillong Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Start your day with a visit to Shillong Peak, where you can enjoy panoramic views of the city and the surrounding Khasi Hills. Next, explore Elephant Falls, one of the most beautiful waterfalls in Shillong. Afterward, head to the Don Bosco Museum to learn more about the culture and traditions of Northeast India. Continue your exploration by visiting the Mawphlang Sacred Forest, a lush green forest of cultural significance to the Khasi tribe. Later, visit Laitlum Canyons, which offers breathtaking views and great photo opportunities. In the evening, enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of Umiam Lake, also known as Barapani, a stunning reservoir just outside Shillong. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Shillong to Cherrapunji (2hrs/60kms)
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, embark on a drive to Cherrapunji (approximately 2-3 hours). Once you arrive, visit Nohkalikai Falls, one of the tallest waterfalls in India. Afterward, explore Mawsmai Cave, a well-lit limestone cave that is easy to explore. Next, visit the Seven Sisters Waterfalls, a series of stunning waterfalls in the region. In the evening, enjoy the cool, misty atmosphere of this hill station and stay overnight in Cherrapunji at a hotel or homestay.

itinerary.title: Cherrapunji Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Start your day with a visit to the famous Living Root Bridges in Nongriat Village. A short trek will lead you to the double-decker root bridge, a rewarding sight. Continue  to Dainthlen Waterfall, one of the most picturesque falls in the area, before heading to Thangkharang Park, which offers stunning views of the plains of Bangladesh. In the evening, relax and enjoy the peaceful ambiance of Cherrapunji. Stay overnight in Cherrapunji.

itinerary.title: Cherrapunji to Mawlynnong & Dawki (2hrs/60kms) – Return to Shillong
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, drive to Mawlynnong Village (approx. 2 hours), known as the cleanest village in Asia. Walk around the village, enjoying its cleanliness and beautiful surroundings. Visit the Sky View in Mawlynnong, a bamboo structure offering panoramic views of the region, including a view of Bangladesh. Continue your journey to Dawki (about 1-1.5 hours), where you can enjoy a boat ride on the Umngot River, famous for its crystal-clear waters. Afterward, return to Shillong by evening and enjoy an overnight stay there.

itinerary.title: Shillong to Kaziranga National Park (5hrs/200kms)
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, check out from your Shillong hotel and drive to Kaziranga National Park, which takes approximately 5 hours. Upon arrival, check in to your resort, freshen up, and relax. You may also enjoy an optional safari or simply relax in the serene environment of your resort. In the evening, enjoy leisure time at the resort or explore the surroundings. Stay overnight in Kaziranga.

itinerary.title: Kaziranga National Park Safari & Departure
itinerary.desc: Start your day with an early morning elephant safari, followed by a jeep safari in the park to spot the famous one-horned rhinoceros, tigers, elephants, and various birds. After the safari, visit the Kaziranga Orchid Park to explore its diverse range of orchids. After breakfast, check out from your hotel and drive back to Guwahati (approx. 5 hours). Upon arrival, transfer to Guwahati Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey.

Enjoy some local delicacies for dinner and stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Shillong Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Start your day with a visit to Shillong Peak, where you can enjoy panoramic views of the city and the surrounding Khasi Hills. Next, explore Elephant Falls, one of the most beautiful waterfalls in Shillong. Afterward, head to the Don Bosco Museum to learn more about the culture and traditions of Northeast India. Continue your exploration by visiting the Mawphlang Sacred Forest, a lush green forest of cultural significance to the Khasi tribe. Later, visit Laitlum Canyons, which offers breathtaking views and great photo opportunities. In the evening, enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of Umiam Lake, also known as Barapani, a stunning reservoir just outside Shillong. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Shillong to Cherrapunji (2hrs/60kms)
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, embark on a drive to Cherrapunji (approximately 2-3 hours). Once you arrive, visit Nohkalikai Falls, one of the tallest waterfalls in India. Afterward, explore Mawsmai Cave, a well-lit limestone cave that is easy to explore. Next, visit the Seven Sisters Waterfalls, a series of stunning waterfalls in the region. In the evening, enjoy the cool, misty atmosphere of this hill station and stay overnight in Cherrapunji at a hotel or homestay.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Cherrapunji Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Start your day with a visit to the famous Living Root Bridges in Nongriat Village. A short trek will lead you to the double-decker root bridge, a rewarding sight. Continue  to Dainthlen Waterfall, one of the most picturesque falls in the area, before heading to Thangkharang Park, which offers stunning views of the plains of Bangladesh. In the evening, relax and enjoy the peaceful ambiance of Cherrapunji. Stay overnight in Cherrapunji.

itinerary.title: Day 5: Cherrapunji to Mawlynnong & Dawki (2hrs/60kms) – Return to Shillong
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, drive to Mawlynnong Village (approx. 2 hours), known as the cleanest village in Asia. Walk around the village, enjoying its cleanliness and beautiful surroundings. Visit the Sky View in Mawlynnong, a bamboo structure offering panoramic views of the region, including a view of Bangladesh. Continue your journey to Dawki (about 1-1.5 hours), where you can enjoy a boat ride on the Umngot River, famous for its crystal-clear waters. Afterward, return to Shillong by evening and enjoy an overnight stay there.

itinerary.title: Day 6: Shillong to Kaziranga National Park (5hrs/200kms)
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, check out from your Shillong hotel and drive to Kaziranga National Park, which takes approximately 5 hours. Upon arrival, check in to your resort, freshen up, and relax. You may also enjoy an optional safari or simply relax in the serene environment of your resort. In the evening, enjoy leisure time at the resort or explore the surroundings. Stay overnight in Kaziranga.

itinerary.title: Day 7: Kaziranga National Park Safari & Departure
itinerary.desc: Start your day with an early morning elephant safari, followed by a jeep safari in the park to spot the famous one-horned rhinoceros, tigers, elephants, and various birds. After the safari, visit the Kaziranga Orchid Park to explore its diverse range of orchids. After breakfast, check out from your hotel and drive back to Guwahati (approx. 5 hours). Upon arrival, transfer to Guwahati Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Leh
itinerary.desc: Arrive at Leh Kushok Bakula Airport. (This must be one of the Most Sensational Flights in the World. On a clear day from one side of the aircraft can be seen in the distance the peaks of K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum and on the other side of the aircraft, so close that you feel you could reach out and touch it, is the Nun Kun massif). Upon arrival you will be met by our representative and transfer to Hotel for check-in. Complete day for rest and leisure to acclimatize to the higher altitude. Overnight stay at Hotel City Palace

itinerary.title: Day Excursion to Matho, Stakna, Stok & Mahabodhi
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, we start on a sightseeing tour visiting Matho Monastery, Stakna Monastery, Stok Palace and Mahabodhi. Matho Monastery: Located around 26 kilometers away from Leh, on the picturesque Indus Valley, Matho Monastery is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery built under the Saskya Monastic Establishment. It was constructed around 500 years ago. Notes : All entrance fees to Monastries and Monuments are on Direct Payment Basis, payable by the customer. Overnight stay at Hotel City Palace

itinerary.title: Excursion to Pangong Lake
itinerary.desc: After an early breakfast, we leave for Pangong Lake through Changla pass (5486 Mtrs). The long easy ascent takes you to Changla pass through its winding roads passing through Sakti Village. Stop at the Changla Pass for a quick photograph session. The Chang La (also known as Changla) is one of the highest mountain roads of the country. The pass, guarded and maintained by the Indian Army (due its proximity to Chinese border), is covered with snow throughout the year. This road is usually open all year, but it can be closed anytime when the access is not cleared of snow. The Changla Pass is the main gateway for the Changthang Plateau situated in the Himalayas. The pass is located on the 134 km-long (83 mi) road between the Pangong Lake and Leh. Road closures can be frequent. Later, we drive down to the village of Tangtse, where you can relax for a cup of tea. Leaving Tangtse for Pangong you pass through few small villages of Changthang and finally you can have a sudden view of the Pangong Lake situated at 14,000 feet (4,267 m). This famous blue brackish Lake of Pangong is 5/6 Kms wide and over 133 Kms long with half of it's running the other side of the "INDO CHINA BORDER". Overnight stay at Hotel City Palace

itinerary.title: Excursion to Nubra Valley
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, we proceed to Nubra Valley. The road journey from Leh to Nubra Valley passes over Khardung La (The Highest Motorable Road In The World). Khardung La: The Highest Motor able Road in The World at 5,602 Mtrs. / 18,390 Ft, around 39 km from Leh. From the pass, one can see all the way south over the Indus valley to seemingly endless peaks and ridges of the Zanskar range, and north to the giants of the Saser massif. The views from the top of the pass are amazing. Later, we visit Hunder and Disket Monastery. Diskit monastery also known as Diskit Gompa is situated in the Nubra valley of Ladakh. This Buddhist center is one of the oldest and largest monasteries in Leh Ladakh. The Diskit monastery was founded by Changzem Tserab Zangpo in the 14th century. The prime attraction of the Diskit monastery is 100 foot high Maitreya Buddha statue, which was inaugurated by the holy Dalai Lama. Overnight stay at Hotel City Palace Notes : All entrance fees to Monastries and Monuments are on Direct Payment Basis, payable by the customer.

itinerary.title: Half Day Excursion to Sham Valley
itinerary.desc: After breakfast drive downstream along the River Indus on Leh - Kargil Highway and start sightseeing with: Hall of Fame: The Hall of Fame, located near the Leh Airfield, is a museum constructed as well as maintained by the Indian Army in the memory of the soldiers who had lost their lives during the Indo-Pak wars. It is also termed as a memorial for the war heros. This building consists of two floors. While on the ground floor, there is information about the brave soldiers and a souvenir shop but on the first floor, there are artifacts of various wars (mainly Kargil war) such as the weapons used during the war and some important documents, related to the same. There is another section dedicated to the Siachen glacier. Gurudwara Patthar Sahib: Situated 25 miles from Leh in Ladakh region in Jammu and Kashmir, Gurudwara Pathar Sahib stands. Overnight stay at Hotel City Palace Notes : All entrance fees to Monastries and Monuments are on Direct Payment Basis, payable by the customer.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Tokyo - The Land of Rising Sun
itinerary.desc: The moment you land in Tokyo, you feel it — this place is different. Bright lights, quiet corners, polite smiles, and a sense of excitement in the air. After settling into your hotel, you have your first evening to soak it all in. Your Japan story begins. (Dinner) Overnight stay at Asakusa View Hotel

itinerary.title: Feeling Tokyo: From Peaceful Shrines to Shibuya Lights
itinerary.desc: Your day begins with the peaceful gardens of the Imperial Palace, the official residence of Japan’s Emperor. As you stroll along green pathways and admire the graceful Nijubashi Bridge from a distance — beautifully curved and uniquely shaped — you’ll feel a quiet calm in the heart of this busy city. Next, you head to the charming Asakusa area, walking past the lively Nakamise shopping street before reaching the beautiful Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo’s oldest Buddhist temple. The sound of prayers, glowing lanterns, and the gentle smell of incense make this moment truly special. Enjoy some free time for lunch before continuing your journey. Later, experience serenity at Meiji Jingu, a Shinto shrine hidden inside a peaceful forest. From here, step into the playful energy of Harajuku — known as a hub of youth culture, fashion experimentation, street style and pop culture. Your day ends at the iconic Shibuya Crossing, the world-famous pedestrian scramble where thousands cross from all directions at once under towering neon lights and digital billboards — a true symbol of Tokyo’s modern spirit. As the evening settles in, you return with quiet smiles, full hearts, and beautiful first memories of Japan. Overnight in Tokyo. (Breakfast and Dinner). Overnight stay at Asakusa View Hotel

itinerary.title: Exploration & Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Mount Fuji & Lake Kawaguchi Experience Today feels like stepping into a postcard. You leave the city behind and travel toward majestic Mount Fuji, Japan’s most loved natural icon. Your first stop is Oishi Park, where gentle breezes and flower-lined paths open up to stunning views of Lake Kawaguchi — part of the Fuji Five Lakes region, famous for its calm waters and mirror-like reflections of the mountain. Next, you visit Arakurayama Sengen Park, home to the iconic Chureito Pagoda and Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine. From here, the views feel truly magical — one of Japan’s most photographed scenes. In Fujiyoshida, enjoy relaxed free time for lunch and browse traditional shops for local souvenirs. Later, discover the peaceful village of Oshino Hakkai, known for its crystal-clear ponds, thatched houses, and quiet countryside charm. Your journey continues up to Mount Fuji’s 5th Station (weather permitting), where fresh mountain air and panoramic views surround you. Standing here, you understand why Fuji is seen as sacred — its perfect shape and quiet presence leave a deep impression. It’s a day filled with scenery, silence, and simple joy — a beautiful contrast to the busy cities. You return to Tokyo carrying mountain memories and a calm heart. Overnight in Tokyo. (Breakfast and Dinner) Overnight stay at Asakusa View Hotel

itinerary.title: Tokyo to Kanazawa
itinerary.desc: Tokyo to Kanazawa - From City Lights to Old Streets Today is a travel day as you move from Tokyo to Kanazawa. After breakfast, you start your journey by Bullet Train. Roughly about 3.5 Hrs, but comfortable, and you’ll notice how the scenery slowly changes from the busy city to quieter towns and open landscapes. Once you reach Kanazawa, the vibe feels different — calmer and more traditional. You first visit the Higashi Chaya District. This area is known for its old wooden houses and traditional tea houses. The streets are narrow and charming, and it really feels like stepping into old Japan. It’s a nice place to walk around, click pictures, and just soak in the atmosphere. Next, you head to Kanazawa Castle. The castle grounds are wide and open, with strong stone walls and beautiful surroundings. It gives you a good sense of the city’s history and its samurai past. In the evening, enjoy dinner at an Indian restaurant and then transfer to your hotel. Overnight in Kanazawa. Overnight stay at Kanazawa Tokyu Hotel

itinerary.title: Finding Your Calm: Torii Gates, Temples & Quiet Kyoto Moments
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, you board the train toward Kyoto. Outside your window, the scenery slowly changes — quiet towns, green landscapes, and soft glimpses of Lake Biwa drifting past like a moving painting. By the time you arrive, Kyoto feels different. Slower. Softer. Older. This is where Japan’s soul quietly lives. Your afternoon begins at Fushimi Inari Taisha, walking through endless red torii gates that wind gently up the hillside. With every step, the world feels quieter — almost meditative — as if time itself has slowed down. Next, you visit Sanjusangen-do, A buddhist temple & home to 1,001 golden statues standing silently in perfect harmony. It’s a powerful, peaceful moment that stays with you long after you leave. Your day ends at Kiyomizu-dera - Pure Water Temple, where you stand on a wooden terrace overlooking Kyoto. As the city stretches out below and the light softens, you simply pause — taking it all in. Kyoto doesn’t rush you. It gently teaches you to slow down. You return to your hotel feeling lighter, calmer, and deeply connected to Japan’s timeless beauty. Overnight in Kyoto. (Breakfast and Dinner) Overnight stay at Hotel Nikko Princess Kyoto

itinerary.title: Exploration & Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Osaka City Experience: Neon Streets & Everyday Life Today, the mood changes. After breakfast, you travel from Kyoto into Osaka — and almost immediately, you feel the difference. This city is louder, brighter, warmer and full of life. You begin in Namba and Dotonbori, where neon lights glow even in daylight and the streets buzz with life. The smell of street food drifts through the air, laughter echoes from small cafés, and everywhere you look, something is happening. Osaka doesn’t try to impress — it simply invites you in. Tucked quietly between busy lanes, you step into Hozenji Temple, a small 17th-century temple where moss covered statues and gentle prayers offer a peaceful calm before the city buzz pulls you back in. Then comes Kuromon Ichiba Market, where locals shop, eat, and laugh. This is where you truly see everyday Osaka — real, friendly, raw and real, and full of flavour and it’s impossible not to love it. Explore the retro neighbourhood of Shinsekai, that feels playful and nostalgic, then admire the grandeur of Osaka Castle, rising proudly above green gardens — a beautiful reminder of Japan’s powerful past. Before leaving, you stroll through the famous shopping streets Shinsaibashi and Nipponbashi, perfect for souvenirs, fashion, and last-minute finds. As evening settles in, you return to Kyoto — carrying Osaka’s colours, flavours, and energy with you. It ’s a day that makes you feel alive. Overnight in Kyoto. (Breakfast and Dinner) Overnight stay at Hotel Nikko Princess Kyoto

itinerary.title: Exploration & Sightseeing
itinerary.desc: Departure: Taking Japan Home in Your Heart After breakfast, it’s time to say goodbye. You complete your check-out and transfer to the airport, carrying more than just souvenirs — you carry memories of glowing streets, quiet temples, mountain breezes, and moments that touched your heart. You didn’t just travel through Japan — you felt it. From quiet temples to glowing streets, this journey becomes a beautiful memory you’ll carry long after you return home. (Breakfast)

itinerary.title: Galle and Bentota Day-Tour
itinerary.desc: Breakfast at hotel. This is a Galle and Bentota Day Tour that includes pick-up from your hotel. The Boat Safari at Madu River is a major attraction that will show you the view of the wide Madu Ganga. It’s a healing journey through the mangrove forest and observe the biodiversity of Madu River that includes 19 endemic species. There are 64 islands and is such an attractive destination for nature lovers and bird watchers. Catch sights of the rare bird species and reptiles that made their home here. There are also traditional fishermen here who make a living through Stilt Fishing. It is a method that uses a crossbar with a vertical pole attached to the sea floor and they wait by the crossbar for the fish to bite. Then visit the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project for turtle hatching. Since 1981, the area has become one of the best locations to find turtles laying their eggs and it was established by the Wildlife Protection Society. The project will take in newborn turtles and raise them in big tanks with nutritional food and clean environment for just a few days. They’ll then be released into the wild at night from the safest area to ensure survivability. The Conservation generally has five species they take care of and visitors will learn all about these gorgeous turtles that are now endangered. They are also allowed to interact with the turtles and hold them in their palms and check out the babies in their tanks. Overnight stay at Courtyard By Marriott Colombo

itinerary.title: Colombo City Tour
itinerary.desc: Colombo is the business and commercial center and the new capital is Sri Jayawardhanapura Kotte, only a few miles away. Colombo was only a small seaport, which came into prominence in the 16th Century with the arrival of the Portuguese in 1505 and the development of it as a major Harbor took place during the British period. Colombo became the capital of Sri Lanka in 1815 after Kandyan Kingdom was ceded to the British. The remains of the buildings during the period of the Portuguese, Dutch and British rule are found in every area of the city. None of the Portuguese & Dutch fortifications are found today but some of their buildings and churches could be seen in the Fort & Pettah areas. Visit Fort, the former British administrative center and military garrison, Sea Street - the Goldsmith’s quarters in the heart of Pettah, the Bazaar area where there is also a Hindu Temple with elaborate stone carvings, the Kayman’s Gate with the Belfry at the original gate to enter the Fort, the Dutch Church of Wolfendhaal dating back to 1749, Kelaniya Buddhist Temple dating to 6th C.B.C., Davatagaha Mosque, Colombo Museum and the Natural History Museum are some of the sites to be visited. Also visit the BMICH (Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall), see the replica of Avukana Buddha in front and the Independence Memorial. Take out time for some shopping before returning back to your hotel. Overnight stay at Courtyard By Marriott Colombo

itinerary.title: Transfer from Colombo to Nuwara Eliya Via Gampola Ambuluwawa Tower
itinerary.desc: After breakfast, depart from Colombo and travel towards Gampola to visit the iconic Ambuluwawa Tower, known for its unique spiral tower and breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. After exploring the hilltop complex, continue your scenic drive through tea plantations and misty landscapes to the charming hill station of Nuwara Eliya, often referred to as “Little England,” then Check in at the hotel. Overnight stay at Heritance Tea Factory

itinerary.title: Sita Amman Temple & Bahirawakanda Temple Tour
itinerary.desc: Enjoy your breakfast today before we set off on our tour of the day. We’re going to Sita Amman Temple as our first destination, a Hindu Temple dedicated to Princess Sita that was also mentioned in the epic of Ramayana. The story goes that Sita was rescued by Rama 5000 years ago and to commemorate her, the temple was built here. Many devotees visit the temple to worship Sita Mata. Visitors are advised to wear modestly when they visit the temple. We’ll then visit the Bahirawakanda Temple, where you can see the popular Bahirawakanda Buddha statue erected atop the Bahirawa Kanda Hill. It is located at the temple, which is also known as Sri Maha Bodhi Temple and is gorgeously sculpted and put up in 1972. Bahirawakanda means “Gnome Mountain” and is a reference to the legend that an evil human-eating gnome used to live here. From the top of the hill, you can get a panoramic view of Kandy city. Visitors need to remove their shoes and hats before entering to offer flowers or oil lamps. We’ll ride back to the hotel in Nuwara Eliya for an overnight stay. itinerary.desc: You will be met by our representative at the Airport Arrival Terminal. Our representative will be holding a signage card with your Name written on it. You will then be escorted to waiting vehicle for transfer to hotel. A daily evening two hour cruise along the man made Dubai Marina for sightseeing of luxurious and modern landmarks which have soured Dubai in the shape of sky touching towers for residential and commercial purpose over the past decade. This cruise is also accompanied by complimentary International Buffet dinner from a five star hotel, soft drinks, mineral water & live entertainment - tanoura dance show. The dhows are fully insured, safety fitted and fully air-conditioned for your safety and enjoyment. Ladies and gents washrooms as well as an open air upper deck are also part of the dhow structure. You can not miss these dhows and you find them elegantly gliding the Marina Promenade and into the open sea where the splendid Palm Island floats in front of you. Overnight stay at Fortune Pearl Hotel, Deira Dinner - Included

itinerary.title: Dubai Frame - Desert Safari
itinerary.desc: Proceed for a visit to the Dubai Frame. The frame measures 150 metres high and 93 metres wide is the latest attraction. The two towers are connected by a 100-squaremetre bridge, which has a 25-square-metre glass panel in the middle offering a great 360 degree view. You can visit a museum on the ground floor that will showcase Dubai’s transformation from fishing village to metropolis. The Evening Desert Safari is a must-do for any adventure seekers visiting Dubai. Convenient round trip transportation will pick you up from your hotel and take you out to explore the Arabian desert. Test your balancing skills in an exhilarating sand boarding experience or try out the other many fun activities available for you to do including camel riding, dune bashing and henna painting. Take time to look around and take pictures, this tour is a great opportunity to capture breathtaking views of the desert during sunset. End the night with belly dancing show under the stars while indulging in a delicious BBQ dinner with unlimited soft drinks and shisha smoking (at extra cost). Ride the quad bikes during desert safari (at extra cost) once you reach the camp. Notes: Please bring a valid Photo ID/passport with you as it is required to be displayed at the entrance. Food and beverage will not be permitted at the Dubai Frame. Please wear respectful attire. Please avoid touching Items displayed in exhibitions. Children under the age of 12 must be accompanied by an adult. The food served on the desert safari camp comes from the catering facility in the city hence it may not be of the best standard Premium Quality food upgrades are available at additional cost. As part of regular seat booked, seating is on cushions around tables. You can upgrade to VIP seating by paying extra directly, which allows you to sit on comfortable cushioned chairs, and have food and drinks served on the table. Dune bashing can get bumpy. For safety purposes, we do not recommend that children aged 0-2, pregnant women or the elderly to take part in this activity Infant seats are not available for dune bashing During the month of Ramadan there will be no belly dance performances or servings of alcohol Please be aware that shared safari experiences involve seating arrangements with other guests, and specific seats (e.g., front or middle) are subject to availability. The last row may also feel slightly cozier compared to other seats. If there are any conditions where auto-assigned seats are not preferred, please consider upgrading to a Private vehicle for an additional charge. Overnight stay at Fortune Pearl Hotel, Deira Breakfast Included at Hotel

itinerary.title: Dubai Mall + Burj Khalifa + Aquarium
itinerary.desc: Transfer to Dubai Mall, one of the largest malls in the world and home to over 1200 stores. Discover Dubai Aquarium and visit the underwater zoo. Rising to the third floor of The Dubai Mall, the aquarium is home to 140 species of sea life and has several ways to experience underwater life, starting with a stroll through a 48-metre walk-through tunnel. It's a complete fish-eye view, with sand tiger sharks and stingrays swimming overhead. Later proceed to the Top of Burj Khalifa, World's Tallest Tower. You will be taken to the 124th Floor Observation Deck at Burj Khalifa from where you can admire panoramic views entire Dubai. Spend half an hour at the top and then come down, and at 7 pm watch the Dubai Fountains come alive. There is a 10 minute show every 20 minutes and its lovely to watch the largest fountain in the world. Overnight stay at Fortune Pearl Hotel, Deira Breakfast - Included at Hotel

itinerary.title: Full Day Abu Dhabi Tour With Ferrari World
itinerary.desc: Proceed for full day tour of Abu Dhabi with Ferrari Theme Park. We start our Abu Dhbai City tour in the morning and our journey will start from Dubai will take you past the Jebel Ali Port, the largest man-made port in the entire world on the road to Abu Dhabi. In the afternoon visit Ferrari World. Ferrari World is Situated on the Yas island, FWAD has a surface area of 200,000 square meters, all under cover, which makes it the biggest indoor park in the world. There are over 20 attractions for visitors to enjoy, from the must futuristic such as Formula Rossa, the worlds fastest rollercoaster, which can accelerate its cars from 0 to 240 kmh in the same time as a Formula 1 car, to the four dimensional Speed of Magic. Return back to hotel in the evening. The best part about Ferrari World is that it has the worlds Fastest Roller Coaster, Formula Rosso. The Flying Aces is a must try. Also, once you arrive there go straight to the go karting game to book your game for the day (tickets run out very fast once the theme park open). Overnight stay at Fortune Pearl Hotel, Deira Breakfast - Included at Hotel

blogs.content:
Why March 8 Is the Perfect Time for a Women's Day Getaway

International Women's Day on March 8, 2026, falls right in the middle of spring in India—a season when the mountains are waking up and the plains are shedding their winter chill. Rather than celebrating with another dinner reservation, why not give yourself or the women in your life something more meaningful? A journey to India's most sacred pilgrimage sites offers not just spiritual renewal, but also the kind of adventure and camaraderie that stays with you long after you return home.


The Himalayan region in March offers the best of both worlds: manageable weather conditions and the spiritual energy of pilgrimage season. Whether you're traveling solo to reconnect with yourself or gathering a group of friends for a shared adventure, there are packages designed specifically to make your Women's Day celebration memorable.


Solo Travel: Embracing Your Own Spiritual Journey

Why Solo Travel Works in March

Traveling alone to a pilgrimage site might sound daunting, but March is actually an ideal time. The weather is stable enough that you won't face extreme conditions, yet the crowds are manageable compared to peak season. You'll have the space to move at your own pace, reflect at your own rhythm, and connect with other pilgrims who are on similar journeys.


Solo travelers often report that pilgrimage journeys change their perspective on independence and self-reliance. You're not just visiting temples; you're proving something to yourself about your own capability and courage.

The Do Dham by Road Package: Perfect for Solo Explorers

The Do Dham Yatra by Road (5 nights, 6 days) is ideal for solo travelers who want a structured yet flexible experience. This package covers the two most sacred sites—Kedarnath and Badrinath—without the extended commitment of the full Char Dham.


What You'll Experience:


  • Day 1: Travel from Haridwar to Guptkashi (205 km, 7-8 hours). Check in and rest.

  • Day 2: Trek 20 km to Kedarnath Temple. The trek passes through pristine valleys with views of snow-capped peaks. You can hire a Doli (traditional palanquin) or horse if needed.

  • Day 3: Early morning darshan at Kedarnath Temple, then trek back to Guptkashi.

  • Days 4-5: Travel to Badrinath (200 km), visit the temple, explore Mana Village, Vyas Gufa, and local sites.

  • Day 6: Return journey to Haridwar via Rishikesh.


Solo Pricing: Starting from ₹26,999 per person (Standard category, 2-person group rate). For a truly solo experience, you'd be in a 2-person vehicle, which costs ₹26,999-₹38,999 depending on accommodation quality.


Why It Works for Solo Travelers:


  • Structured itinerary removes decision fatigue

  • Professional guides and drivers handle logistics

  • Shared accommodations mean you can meet other travelers if you want company

  • Flexible meal times and rest periods

  • No pressure to keep pace with a group


Group Travel: Celebrating Together

Why Group Travel Amplifies the Experience

Women's Day is about celebrating the strength, resilience, and bond between women. Traveling as a group—whether it's friends, colleagues, or family—transforms a pilgrimage into a shared memory. You'll laugh together during the trek, support each other through the challenging moments, and return home with stories that will keep you connected for years.


Group travel also offers practical advantages: shared vehicle costs, the ability to customize your experience, and the safety of traveling with people you know and trust.

The Do Dham by Road Package: Best for Group Bonding

For groups of 4-6 women, the Do Dham by Road package offers the best value and flexibility.


Group Pricing (4 people in Innova Crysta):


  • Standard: ₹24,999 per person

  • Deluxe: ₹26,999 per person

  • Luxury: ₹29,999 per person

  • Premium: ₹35,999 per person


What Makes It Group-Friendly:


  • Shared vehicle means you're together throughout the journey

  • Bonding happens naturally during long drives and shared meals

  • You can hire Doli/horses together for the trek, making it a shared challenge

  • Accommodations are on twin/double sharing basis, so you can room with your travel companions

  • Vegetarian meals are served at fixed times, creating natural gathering moments


Sample Group Itinerary for 4 Women:


  • Book 2 rooms (twin sharing) at each location

  • Share one Innova Crysta vehicle throughout

  • Hire horses or Doli together for the Kedarnath trek

  • Explore local sites as a group in the evenings

  • Total cost per person: ₹24,999-₹35,999 depending on category


The Char Dham Option: For the Committed Pilgrim

When to Choose Char Dham Over Do Dham

If your group has more time and wants the complete spiritual experience, the Char Dham by Road (9 nights, 10 days) covers all four sacred sites: Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath. This is the traditional pilgrimage route and holds deep significance in Hindu spirituality.


Char Dham Pricing (4 people in Innova Crysta):


  • Standard: ₹37,999 per person

  • Deluxe: ₹43,999 per person

  • Luxury: ₹48,999 per person

  • Premium: ₹57,999 per person


What's Included:


  • 2 nights in Barkot (Yamunotri base)

  • 2 nights in Uttarkashi (Gangotri base)

  • 2 nights in Guptkashi (Kedarnath base)

  • 1 night at Kedarnath (basic ashram accommodation)

  • 1 night in Badrinath

  • 1 night in Rudraprayag

  • All meals (breakfast and dinner, vegetarian)

  • AC vehicle with experienced driver

  • All tolls and parking charges


Two Treks in Char Dham:


  • Yamunotri: 5 km trek (can hire Doli/horse)

  • Kedarnath: 20 km trek (can hire Doli/horse)


The Char Dham journey is more demanding physically and time-wise, but many women report it as a transformative experience that deepens their spiritual connection and personal growth.


The Helicopter Option: For Time-Constrained Travelers

Do Dham by Helicopter: Same-Day Experience

If you have limited time but want to visit both Kedarnath and Badrinath, the Do Dham by Helicopter (Same Day) is a luxury option priced at ₹125,000 per person (inclusive of all costs).


What's Included:


  • VIP darshan at both Kedarnath and Badrinath temples

  • Total weight limit of 445 kg for all passengers

  • Timings are subject to weather and flight permissions

  • Passengers should carry exact body weight measured on electronic scale


This option is ideal for women who want the spiritual experience without the physical demands of trekking, or those with tight schedules.


Practical Tips for Women Travelers

What to Pack

March weather in the Himalayas ranges from 5-15°C depending on altitude. Pack layers: thermal wear, fleece jackets, and a waterproof outer layer. Comfortable trekking shoes are essential for the Kedarnath trek. Bring a small medical kit with pain relievers, altitude sickness medication, and any personal medications.

Accommodation Standards

All packages use verified hotels with attached bathrooms and hot water. Kedarnath is the exception—basic ashram accommodation is provided on a sharing basis. This is part of the authentic pilgrimage experience, and many women find it meaningful.

Safety and Support

Comfort Journey provides experienced guides and drivers who are familiar with the routes and local conditions. Female travelers often appreciate having female guides available upon request. The company handles all logistics, so you can focus on the experience rather than logistics.

Booking Timeline

March 8 is just one week away. If you're interested in traveling around Women's Day, book immediately. The standard booking policy requires 50% deposit at booking, with the balance due 30 days before departure. However, given the proximity to March 8, you may need to discuss expedited booking options with Comfort Journey directly.


Making Your Decision

Choose Solo Travel If:


  • You want time for personal reflection and spiritual connection

  • You prefer flexibility in your daily schedule

  • You're comfortable with independent decision-making

  • You want to meet other pilgrims and make new connections


Choose Group Travel If:


  • You want to celebrate with women who matter to you

  • You prefer shared experiences and mutual support

  • You want to split vehicle costs and make it more economical

  • You value the memories created together


Choose Char Dham If:


  • You have 9-10 days available

  • You want the complete spiritual experience of all four sacred sites

  • You're willing to do two treks

  • You want the traditional pilgrimage route


Choose Helicopter If:


  • You have only 1-2 days available

  • You want to avoid trekking

  • Budget is not a constraint

  • You want a luxury experience with VIP darshans


Final Thoughts

Women's Day 2026 offers a unique opportunity to celebrate yourself or the women in your life in a way that goes beyond typical celebrations. A pilgrimage to the Himalayas—whether solo or with a group—is an investment in spiritual growth, personal strength, and lasting memories. The mountains have a way of putting things in perspective and reminding us of our own resilience.


Whether you choose the manageable 5-day Do Dham journey or the comprehensive 9-day Char Dham experience, you'll return home transformed. And isn't that the best way to celebrate Women's Day?


Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is March 8 too early to visit the Himalayas? A: No. March is actually ideal. The weather is stable, roads are open, and crowds are manageable. Early March can have occasional snow, but it rarely blocks major routes.


Q: Can I travel solo safely? A: Yes. Comfort Journey provides experienced guides and drivers. Many solo women travelers use these packages every year. The pilgrimage sites are well-established with good infrastructure.


Q: What if I can't do the full trek? A: You can hire a Doli (traditional palanquin) or horse for the Kedarnath trek. This is a common option and doesn't diminish the spiritual experience.


Q: Is accommodation comfortable? A: Road packages use verified hotels with attached bathrooms and hot water. Kedarnath is basic ashram accommodation, which is part of the authentic experience. Helicopter packages include premium hotels.
